items.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: I did one beautiful quartet date with Art Farmer called “Perception” with Roy McCurdy, Tommy Williams and myself.

ctx.x: And were you still single at the time?

I’m still single at the time, yeah. So then when I got with the Jazztet, that was, as a matter of fact there’s a book out now that was put out by the Baroness Rothschild called © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

Musicians’ Three Wishes. And she would go around with a camera and ask the musicians if they had three wishes what would that be. And come to find out I’m in the book. I never had no idea. I don’t even recall her or anybody talking to me. Because see here again, I would go to hear Thelonious Monk I would sit at the table with the band but I was well reserved and I knew how to keep my mouth shut and not speak until I was spoken to. items.title: Roy McCurdy interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: We used to work together a long time ago with Harold Mabern and Bob Cranshaw.

ctx.x: Who else was on the band at that time?

Harold Mabern was the piano player. The bass player was a Tommy Williams — I don’t know if you know Tommy Williams — he was a wonderful, wonderful bass player. And he wound up, he was driving a taxi cab in New York a lot, you know, instead of playing steady. But he just played so great. Tommy Williams, myself, Grachan Moncur III, the trombone player, and that was it, and Art and Benny and myself.
Did that band record? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -4-
